the client's structure, staffing or platform changes between discovery and signature
a quote is revised after signature because of a discovery gap

base.update_signal: a delivered engagement that needed a fact the discovery template did not ask for, or a post-signature quote revision traced to a discovery gap

nodes.definition: Build the licence mix from a role inventory rather than from a headcount, and give every seat a written reason for its tier. The method: enumerate the actual humans and what each one does, the owner who lives in mail and documents, office staff, field or shift workers who need little more than mail and a calendar on a phone, contractors, and people who need an identity but no live mailbox; separate out the non-person objects a headcount wrongly counts as users, the shared enquiries address, role addresses, aliases, and room or equipment resources; map each role to the least tier that meets a documented need; and record, for every seat above the base tier, the specific requirement, obligation or observed incident that justifies it. Departed staff are handled by the least-cost route the platform allows rather than by leaving a paid seat running quietly for a year. The output is a per-seat table the client can read in a minute, where every line carries a reason, which is simultaneously the ethical control against over-selling and the reason renewal conversations do not turn into arguments.

included: the role inventory and its separation from non-person objects
mapping each role to the least sufficient tier with a documented reason
handling of leavers and dormant accounts at quote time
the client-readable per-seat table
excluded: monthly seat administration, true-ups and leaver processing in the running relationship, owned by the subscription-management KB
the tenant configuration that implements the mix, owned by the setup-and-migration KB

pros.claim: A per-seat table with a reason on every line converts the licensing conversation from a negotiation into a review
pros.example: an owner reading that four field technicians sit on the lightest tier because they need only mail and a phone calendar, and agreeing in under a minute

pros.claim: Right-sizing at the quote stage prevents the slow accumulation of paid seats nobody uses
pros.example: catching three addresses belonging to people who left the previous year before they are ever billed to the client

cons.claim: Right-sizing downward reduces the operator's own recurring margin and can push a small account below its cost to serve
cons.example: an eleven-address enquiry resolving into seven paid seats plus four shared or resource objects, shrinking the monthly line accordingly

cons.claim: A finely differentiated mix is cheaper monthly but costs more administrative time at every joiner and leaver
cons.example: four different tiers across nine people, each with its own handling when somebody is hired

failure_modes: pricing from an address list, so shared and role mailboxes are sold as paid seats
standardising the whole company on one tier because uniformity is easier to administer
upgrading a tier on a general worry rather than on a documented need
leaving departed staff on paid seats because nobody looked
acceptance_tests: every seat line carries the role and the documented reason for its tier
non-person mail objects are listed separately and are not billed as paid seats
at least one downgrade or no-cost alternative was considered and its outcome recorded
revisit_triggers: the client's headcount, roles or working pattern change
a tier boundary moves in the vendor's licensing
a review finds seats with no current documented reason

base.update_signal: a change in the client's roles or headcount, a vendor tier-boundary move, or a review finding seats without a documented reason

nodes.definition: Model the account rather than the seat, because a per-seat margin that looks healthy multiplied by six seats can still lose money against one support call a week. The model adds the recurring legs, gross margin on resold seats plus the management fee, and subtracts the real cost to serve: the operator's measured support and administration minutes valued at a rate that absorbs non-billable time, the tooling the operator pays for per client or per seat including its own management, security and backup subscriptions, payment processing, provider platform charges, a bad-debt allowance, and any onboarding cost that was under-recovered at the setup stage. The outputs are a per-account contribution and a floor, the minimum monthly amount below which an account is not worth carrying, expressed as a base management fee rather than as a licensing upsell. Every input comes from the operator's own records, because a quarter of honestly logged support minutes is worth more than any published benchmark, and the model is re-run whenever the book's shape changes, since concentration in one large account is a risk the per-seat view never shows.

included: per-account contribution and the cost-to-serve inputs behind it
the account floor expressed as a base fee
measurement discipline from the operator's own records
concentration risk across the book
excluded: the per-deal licence margin computation, which is its own work unit
retention economics, churn modelling and reactivation, owned by the subscription-management KB

pros.claim: A measured cost-to-serve turns 'that client feels like a lot of work' into a number the operator can act on
pros.example: discovering that the two smallest accounts consume more support minutes between them than the largest one

pros.claim: Expressing the floor as a base fee keeps the remedy for a thin account honest instead of turning it into an upsell
pros.example: raising a four-seat account to a stated minimum monthly fee rather than proposing security tiers it does not need

cons.claim: The measurement is a discipline a small operator rarely sustains, and an unmeasured model is just an opinion in a spreadsheet
cons.example: a support log abandoned during a heavy migration month, leaving that quarter's cost data unusable

cons.claim: A floor honestly applied will lose small clients the operator likes and would have carried out of goodwill
cons.example: a long-standing three-seat client declining the minimum fee and moving to self-service

failure_modes: counting margin without subtracting the support duty that produced it
setting a floor and then quietly breaking it for every likeable prospect
repairing a below-floor account by selling licences instead of by pricing the work
ignoring concentration risk while one client grows into most of the book
acceptance_tests: cost-to-serve inputs come from the operator's own logged minutes and invoices, with the measurement period stated
every account below the floor has a recorded decision to re-price, restructure or exit
the model states each client's share of total recurring revenue so concentration is visible
revisit_triggers: a quarter of support-minute data lands
provider platform fees, tooling costs or payment costs change
one client's share of recurring revenue crosses the operator's concentration limit

base.update_signal: a new quarter of measured support minutes, a change in tooling or platform costs, or a shift in revenue concentration

nodes.definition: Derive the one-time fee from the scope drivers that actually consume hours, and make it cover its own cost. The drivers, all discoverable before quoting: the number of real mailboxes and how much history each carries; the source platform, because moving from a hosted mail service, a consumer webmail account, an on-premises server or another suite are four different jobs with different tooling and different failure modes; shared mailboxes, distribution lists, calendars, contacts and any legacy shared-folder structure; domain and record control, including whether anyone can actually reach the registrar; devices and how many people need reconfiguring; the cutover window and whether it must fall outside working hours; the training and hand-holding the staff will need, which for a firm that has never used a real suite is the largest hidden driver; and the documentation deliverable. The fee is computed from measured hours per driver at the operator's own rate, plus third-party tooling, plus a contingency for the unknowns discovery flagged. The discipline that matters is refusing to discount the setup leg into the recurring leg, because a migration financed by future subscription margin is an unsecured loan to a client who is free to leave, and some will.

included: the scope drivers that consume hours and how each is measured
the computation from measured hours, tooling and contingency
the rule against financing setup out of recurring margin
what the fee explicitly excludes
excluded: the execution of the migration itself and its technical sequencing, owned by the setup-and-migration KB
project work billed later in the relationship, owned by the subscription-management KB

pros.claim: A driver-based fee explains itself to the client and defends the number without becoming a discount negotiation
pros.example: showing that the fee rises because the source platform forces a slower mailbox-by-mailbox transfer, rather than presenting a round number

pros.claim: Charging the setup leg at cost or better means the business survives a client who leaves in the first year
pros.example: a client acquired and consolidated six months after a migration, where the setup fee had already covered its hours

cons.claim: Driver-based quoting is slower than a per-mailbox rule of thumb and can price the operator out of simple jobs competitors quote in a minute
cons.example: losing a straightforward five-mailbox move to a flat-rate competitor while still working through discovery

cons.claim: The largest driver, training an office that has never used a real suite, is the hardest one to estimate honestly
cons.example: a firm where every one of nine staff needs individual hand-holding on a phone as well as a desktop

failure_modes: quoting from mailbox count alone and meeting the shared folders and archives on the weekend
waiving the setup fee to win the recurring contract and never recovering the hours
excluding after-hours cutover from the quote and then performing it anyway
carrying no contingency for the items discovery explicitly marked unknown
acceptance_tests: the quote lists the scope drivers with the hours assumed for each and names what is excluded
the fee covers measured cost at the operator's own rate before any discount is even considered
unknowns flagged in discovery appear as a named contingency rather than as silent optimism
revisit_triggers: actual migration hours diverge materially from the quoted assumption on a driver
a tooling change makes a driver materially cheaper or more expensive
a source platform appears that the driver list does not cover

base.update_signal: delivered migration hours diverging from the quoted drivers, or a tooling change that alters the cost of a driver

nodes.definition: Assemble everything the business has decided into one offer a small-business owner can read in a few minutes and be bound by. It states the per-seat table with the reason for each tier; the setup fee with its scope drivers and its explicit exclusions; what the management fee includes month to month and what is billed separately; the term and cancellation structure, which must mirror the commitment term actually purchased from the provider rather than the flexibility the operator wishes it could offer; the compensation disclosure and the client's direct-purchase alternative; what the client owns, including the tenant, the domain and the data, and how each is handed back; the support channel and pattern as promised at sale; and a price validity date tied to the price list the quote was built from. Two mismatches are fatal and both are checked here, promising a cancellation right the purchased licence term cannot deliver, and promising support that neither the program nor the operator's staffing can back. The offer is the boundary object between selling and delivering: the running support model and the monthly administration it points toward belong to the later stages of the business rather than to this document.

included: everything the offer must state before signature
term mirroring between what is sold and what is bought
disclosure, ownership and handback statements at sale time
the price validity date and its link to the quoted price list
excluded: the operating support model, response targets and escalation practice in the running relationship, owned by the subscription-management KB
the delivery schedule and migration runbook, owned by the setup-and-migration KB

pros.claim: One readable document stating term, inclusions, exclusions and ownership ends most of the disputes this business is capable of having
pros.example: a client questioning a project charge and finding that exact exclusion listed in the offer they signed

pros.claim: Mirroring the term prevents the single most expensive sales mistake, selling flexibility the operator has already bought away
pros.example: quoting the flexible structure at its true rate instead of promising monthly cancellation on top of a committed term

cons.claim: A complete offer takes longer to produce than a price in an email, and some prospects read the exclusions as coldness
cons.example: a two-page offer losing momentum against a competitor's single monthly figure sent within the hour

failure_modes: promising monthly cancellation on top of a committed annual term the operator cannot exit
leaving the management fee's inclusions undefined so that every future request is arguable
issuing an offer with no price validity date after a price list has already moved
omitting the ownership and handback statement, which is exactly the fear the buyer arrived with
acceptance_tests: the cancellation terms offered are executable against the licence terms actually purchased from the provider
inclusions, exclusions, ownership and handback, support channel, compensation disclosure and a price validity date all appear in the document
the seat table in the offer matches the right-sizing output line for line
revisit_triggers: a provider term or price change invalidates an outstanding offer
a dispute reveals a term the offer failed to state
the support promise in the offer proves unstaffable in practice

base.update_signal: a provider term or price change affecting outstanding offers, or a dispute exposing a term the offer template omitted

edges.why_related: which program routes are even worth mapping follows from what the business has decided it sells
the segments worth pursuing are the ones whose pain matches the thing the thesis says is being sold
the invoice-ownership decision is a choice between the routes the topology map enumerates
the duties that attach to the operator are defined by the route it transacts under
the register exists to keep the topology snapshot and its terms current rather than remembered
per-seat margin only exists at all in the routes where the operator holds the invoice
the margin computation consumes the dated price list and term structure the register maintains
the authorization document records the specific roles the least-privilege practice has decided to hold
the obligation classes named for a client decide what the authorization must explicitly cover and exclude
the triggers worth watching are the ones that fire inside the chosen segments
the anchor is chosen from what the target segments actually depend on rather than from preference
the licence map is built for the anchor suite, and depth in it is the return on having chosen one
discovery collects the dependency facts the fit diagnosis needs and records its conclusion
a role can only be mapped to the least sufficient tier if the tier boundaries and no-cost alternatives are known
the role inventory that right-sizing consumes is produced by discovery, not by an address list
every scope driver in the setup fee is a fact the discovery record supplies or explicitly marks unknown
account contribution starts from the per-seat margin the mechanism computes and then subtracts cost to serve
what must be disclosed is precisely the compensation structure the margin mechanism describes
the offer carries the setup fee together with the drivers and exclusions that produced it
the seat table in the offer is the right-sizing output, line for line, with its reasons attached
discovery may establish who holds access and who may grant it, but it may not collect credentials or open data before authorization exists
a client's asserted regulated data class constrains which suites, tiers and configurations may honestly be proposed at all
a seat may only be placed above the base tier on a documented need, which is the evidence standard this rule imposes
what the offer may promise about price, term and cancellation is bounded by the terms actually purchasable on the day
discovery must surface the disqualifying facts early enough to stop a deal before the operator has invested a quote in it
margin rises with higher tiers and more seats while the honest recommendation frequently lowers both
edges.resolution_rule: the client's documented need decides the tier; when margin and need disagree, need wins, the smaller configuration is quoted, and the margin foregone is noted in the recommendation log rather than argued about with the client

edges.why_related: right-sizing a small client downward can drop the account below the measured cost-to-serve floor
edges.resolution_rule: never restore a below-floor account by adding licences the client does not need; restore it with a transparent base management fee, restructure the service, or decline the account

edges.why_related: the operator's depth sits in one suite while a given client's dependencies point at the other
edges.resolution_rule: fit evidence wins for the client's outcome; if the misfit is material and the operator cannot deliver the other suite competently, refer the deal out with the reason stated rather than forcing the anchor

edges.why_related: disclosing that the operator earns margin can weaken the trusted-adviser framing in the moment it is being established
edges.resolution_rule: disclose anyway, early and in writing; a position that survives disclosure is the only trusted-operator position worth holding, and a concealed one fails the first time an accountant asks

edges.why_related: an urgent trigger such as a dead mail server pressures the operator to skip discovery and quote a fast cheap setup
edges.resolution_rule: urgency may compress the format of discovery but never remove its scope drivers; issue a bounded emergency scope with a stated re-quote point once the facts are known, rather than a guess dressed as a firm price

edges.why_related: the trigger that created the deal predicts the migration's shape, so it moves the scope drivers before discovery even begins
first-line support duty is the largest single driver of cost to serve and is what makes very small accounts unprofitable
the offer is written only after the discovery record is complete, because every figure in it depends on a fact from that record
the signed offer precedes the authorization record, which is the final gate before any tenant work begins
measured cost to serve on live accounts feeds back into which prospect classes are declined next quarter
which version of the accountability message actually lands tells the operator which segment's pain is genuinely acute and re-ranks the target list
both are the same move applied at different scales, matching a client's documented requirements to the least sufficient product decision, and both fail the same way when decided from a template

conflict_axes.name: honest_right_sizing_vs_seat_margin
conflict_axes.description: The licence mix that best serves the client is frequently the one that pays the operator least, and the same person makes both the recommendation and the margin.
poles: recommend the least sufficient licence for each role
recommend the tier that maximises the spread
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the documented need sets the tier, the margin foregone is logged, and the operator's labour is priced in a management fee that does not move with the tier

conflict_axes.name: anchor_depth_vs_client_fit
conflict_axes.description: Depth in one suite is the small operator's main asset, but some clients inside the target segments genuinely belong on the other one.
poles: keep every client on the anchor suite
follow the fit evidence into the other suite
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: fit evidence decides the client's outcome; where the operator cannot deliver the other suite competently it refers the deal rather than forcing the anchor and learning on the client's data

conflict_axes.name: transacting_control_vs_referral_simplicity
conflict_axes.description: Owning the invoice creates margin, price control and continuity but imports credit risk, collections, tax treatment and first-line support duty; referring keeps life simple and gives away the recurring leg.
poles: transact and carry the billing and support
refer and stay out of the billing chain
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decide once for the whole book against the operator's tolerance for credit risk and support load, and take the referral route deliberately for prospects whose size can never justify carrying them

conflict_axes.name: committed_term_price_vs_client_flexibility
conflict_axes.description: The better unit price generally requires a commitment the operator cannot exit, while the client wants to be able to shrink or leave at any time.
poles: buy the committed term for the better rate
keep the client free to cancel monthly
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: quote both structures with their true rates and consequences and mirror in the offer exactly the term that was purchased, never selling a cancellation right that cannot be executed upstream

conflict_axes.name: speed_of_close_vs_discovery_completeness
conflict_axes.description: Trigger-driven buyers want a number today, while the number depends on facts that take a conversation and sometimes a look at the current environment to establish.
poles: quote immediately from a seat count
quote only from a complete discovery record
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: issue an explicitly labelled budgetary range fast and make the firm figure contingent on the discovery record, with a bounded emergency scope where a real outage is in progress

conflict_axes.name: access_convenience_vs_least_privilege
conflict_axes.description: Standing global rights in every tenant make routine work instant, and they also make the operator the single most dangerous account in every client's business.
poles: hold standing global administration for speed
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: least privilege wins without exception; the friction it creates is absorbed by planning routine work and by naming a deputy approver, never by keeping a permanent global account

conflict_axes.name: book_growth_vs_cost_to_serve
conflict_axes.description: Every small account adds recurring revenue and a support surface, and the smallest ones often consume the most attention per unit of margin they return.
poles: take every small client to grow the book
hold an account floor and decline below it
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry a measured floor expressed as a base management fee, apply it consistently, and treat a below-floor prospect as a pricing decision rather than as a licensing opportunity

conflict_axes.name: adviser_framing_vs_compensation_disclosure
conflict_axes.description: The trusted-operator position depends on the client believing the advice is independent, while the operator is in fact paid more when the client buys more.
poles: keep the compensation model quiet to preserve authority
disclose the margin and the direct-purchase option up front
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclose first and in writing, then advise; authority that requires the client's ignorance is a liability that matures at the worst possible moment

conflict_axes.name: real_security_urgency_vs_fear_selling
conflict_axes.description: Some clients genuinely need a control today and will not act without being told plainly, and the same language used to move them is the language of fear-selling.
poles: press hard on risk to move the buyer
state the risk once, plainly, and let evidence decide
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: describe the client's own situation and the specific requirement, state what the control does and does not prevent, record the decision, and never re-raise a decline without a new fact

edge_cases.description: A prospect is an eligible nonprofit or charity that can obtain donated or heavily discounted licensing, which removes most of the per-seat margin from the deal
edge_cases.trigger: a charity, church or community organisation enquiry where the vendor operates an eligibility program
edge_cases.mitigation: tell them the eligibility exists and help them verify it, move the revenue onto a stated management fee and the setup leg, and decline the work openly if that fee is not acceptable rather than quietly steering them to paid seats

edge_cases.description: The provider announces a price-list revision or a commitment-term restructure while proposals are outstanding
edge_cases.trigger: a change notice with an effective date that falls before the open quotes would be signed
edge_cases.mitigation: every quote carries a validity date and a pass-through statement; re-pull the price list on the day of order and reissue affected proposals rather than absorbing the difference silently for a full term

edge_cases.description: The client already bought licences directly from the vendor on a company card and wants management only
edge_cases.trigger: an existing direct subscription discovered during qualification
edge_cases.mitigation: price management so that it stands on its own without the licence spread, discuss transferring billing only on its own merits with the term consequences stated, and never make support or access conditional on moving the subscription

edge_cases.description: A prospect's mailbox data falls into a regulated class that requires agreements or configurations the operator cannot responsibly provide
edge_cases.trigger: the client states a health, legal, financial or card-payment data class, or a customer contract imposes a security standard
edge_cases.mitigation: name the obligation class in writing, require the client to confirm the requirement with their own advisers in their own jurisdiction, and decline or partner rather than promising a compliance outcome the operator cannot stand behind

edge_cases.description: The person offering administrative credentials has no authority to grant them, or the only holder is a departing IT person
edge_cases.trigger: an office manager hands over a global administrator password, or the outgoing technician is the sole account holder
edge_cases.mitigation: stop and obtain authorization from a named signer with authority to bind the business, document the handover of any inherited credential, and rotate everything inherited before work proceeds

edge_cases.description: An owner asks the operator to open a departing employee's mailbox and show them what was sent
edge_cases.trigger: a termination, a suspected leak, or an internal dispute at the client
edge_cases.mitigation: content access only on a specific written authorization from an authorized signer, logged with its scope and reason, with the employment and data-protection obligation classes named and the client directed to their own advisers; never browse casually and never act on a verbal request

edge_cases.description: The seat count is inflated because shared, role and alias addresses were counted as users
edge_cases.trigger: a quote built from an exported address list rather than from a role inventory
edge_cases.mitigation: split the inventory into humans, shared mailboxes, aliases and resource objects before any pricing, and show the client the split so the reduction is visibly the operator's doing

edge_cases.description: The client demands monthly cancellation while the price quoted assumes a committed term the operator cannot exit
edge_cases.trigger: a flexibility request arriving at signature after the proposal was built on the committed rate
edge_cases.mitigation: requote on the flexible structure at its true rate and let the client choose; never promise a cancellation right that cannot be executed against the licences actually purchased

edge_cases.description: The presenting complaint is a deliverability failure caused by records the client's web host controls, not by the mail platform
edge_cases.trigger: a prospect reports that their quotations and invoices are landing in customers' spam folders
edge_cases.mitigation: diagnose the cause before selling a migration, state plainly which part a migration would and would not fix, and refer or scope the records work separately rather than letting the client believe a new suite solves it

edge_cases.description: The prospect's current arrangement genuinely fits and a migration would add no value this year
edge_cases.trigger: the fit diagnosis finds no material gap between the current environment and what would be proposed
edge_cases.mitigation: say so in writing with the reasoning, offer a bounded review or administration engagement only if the client wants one, and record the no-sale as a proof asset for future conversations

edge_cases.description: A two-person business insists on an enterprise-grade security tier after reading a news story about a breach
edge_cases.trigger: client-initiated over-buying driven by fear rather than by a documented requirement
edge_cases.mitigation: document what the tier does and does not do for a business of that shape, propose the least sufficient tier alongside the practices that actually reduce their risk, and if the client still insists record their decision and the advice given

workflow.description: State what is sold, the two revenue legs, the administrative duty accepted, and what the business does not sell
workflow.gate: both revenue legs, the duty accepted with administrative access and at least three explicit non-offerings are stated

workflow.action: Map the program routes and choose the transacting route
workflow.description: Enumerate the indirect, direct-bill and referral classes with their duties and pick the one this business will operate under
workflow.artifact: dated program topology map with a route decision
workflow.gate: each class names who invoices, who carries credit risk, who answers first and how delegated access is obtained, and the chosen route names its collection and suspension policy

workflow.action: Build the dated program terms register
workflow.description: Record price lists, term options, cancellation windows, caps, eligibility, incentives, access mechanics and notice periods with dates, sources and re-check cadences
workflow.gate: every entry carries a checked date, a named source and a cadence, and stale entries are marked unknown rather than current

workflow.action: Derive the margin worksheet and the support obligation stack
workflow.description: Compute margin from a same-day price list less payment, platform and bad-debt costs, and write the three tiers of support duty that the margin pays for
workflow.artifact: margin worksheet plus a three-tier support duty statement
workflow.gate: the worksheet cites a dated price list and subtracts all costs before naming a margin, and no unearned incentive is treated as revenue

workflow.action: Set the access, authorization and obligation-class discipline
workflow.description: Define least-privilege and time-bound access, identity separation, logging, the revocation path, and the obligation classes that must be named per client
workflow.artifact: access and authorization policy with an obligation-class checklist
workflow.gate: the policy forbids standing global rights, defines the revocation path, and lists the obligation classes to be named and routed for verification in each deal

workflow.action: Choose the anchor suite and the policy for the other
workflow.description: Decide from segment dependencies and honest self-assessment which suite the practice will be deep in, and how prospects belonging on the other are handled
workflow.artifact: anchor decision with a written second-suite policy
workflow.gate: the decision cites segment evidence and the second-suite policy states support, refer or take-with-learning-cost

workflow.action: Build the licence family and tier map
workflow.description: Record tier boundaries, add-ons versus step-ups, frontline and identity-only options, caps, eligibility, mixing rules and downgrade consequences, each with a verification date
workflow.artifact: dated licence map with no-cost alternatives
workflow.gate: every entry is dated and sourced to current vendor documentation and the no-cost alternatives to a paid seat are listed

workflow.action: Define the target segments, trigger watchlist and disqualification rules
workflow.description: Write the segments with observable signals, the triggers that convert them, and the standing rules for declining work
workflow.artifact: target segment sheet with trigger watchlist and decline rules
workflow.gate: each segment has at least two observable signals with implied seat range and support intensity, and each decline rule names its evidence test and its response

workflow.action: Run qualifying discovery on the prospect
workflow.description: Collect the people-versus-objects inventory, platform, domain control, applications, devices, admin holders, asserted data classes, blackout windows and decision path, and run the decline rules and the fit diagnosis
workflow.artifact: prospect discovery record with a fit conclusion
workflow.gate: humans are separated from non-person objects, domain control and the authorized signer are identified, unknowns are listed as contingency, and no decline rule has fired unanswered

workflow.action: Right-size the licence mix and test the account economics
workflow.description: Map each role to the least sufficient tier with a documented reason, then check the resulting account against the measured cost-to-serve floor and derive the setup fee from its scope drivers
workflow.artifact: per-seat table with reasons, account contribution check and setup fee derivation
workflow.gate: every seat line has a reason, at least one downgrade or no-cost alternative was considered, the account clears the floor or has a recorded pricing decision, and the setup fee covers measured cost

workflow.action: Package, disclose and gate the offer
workflow.description: Assemble the seat table, fees, inclusions and exclusions, mirrored term, compensation disclosure, ownership and handback, support channel and price validity, then obtain the signed authorization record before any tenant work
workflow.artifact: signed offer plus signed administrative authorization record
workflow.gate: the cancellation terms are executable against the licences purchased, the disclosure and ownership statements are present, the price validity date is set, and a current authorization record naming signer, roles, envelope and revocation path is on file

dominance_rules.rule: Documented authorization and least privilege dominate delivery convenience and client urgency
dominance_rules.rationale: administrative access to a small business's mail and identity plane is a fiduciary-grade responsibility, and no schedule pressure changes what an unauthorized action is
dominance_rules.trigger: any request to act inside a tenant or on client data without a current written authorization covering that action
dominance_rules.action: stop, obtain authorization from the named signer scoped to the task, and record it before proceeding

dominance_rules.rule: The client's documented need dominates margin whenever the two disagree about a licence tier
dominance_rules.rationale: the operator is the only party in the room able to evaluate the recommendation, and advice bent toward the spread destroys the position the whole business rests on
dominance_rules.trigger: the tier that pays best exceeds what the documented need justifies
dominance_rules.action: quote the least sufficient tier, record the margin foregone in the recommendation log, and state the upgrade path with the condition that would trigger it

dominance_rules.rule: A dated provider-confirmed price or term dominates any remembered, published or competitor-quoted figure
dominance_rules.rationale: program terms are vendor property and are restructured without notice to the operator's memory
dominance_rules.trigger: any quote, renewal figure, margin claim or client promise involving price, term, cap or cancellation
dominance_rules.action: re-pull the current price list and terms before the number leaves the operator's hands and stamp the quote with its source date and validity

dominance_rules.rule: Verified per-client fit evidence dominates the operator's anchor-suite preference
dominance_rules.rationale: an anchor exists to make the operator better at serving clients, not to make clients fit the operator
dominance_rules.trigger: the fit diagnosis contradicts the anchor suite for a specific prospect
dominance_rules.action: follow the evidence; where the operator cannot deliver the other suite competently, refer the deal with the reason stated rather than migrating a client onto a platform it is learning on

dominance_rules.rule: Disclosure dominates persuasion: compensation and alternatives are stated before the recommendation
dominance_rules.rationale: a conflict that is disclosed can be judged by the client, while one that is discovered later ends the relationship regardless of how good the advice was
dominance_rules.trigger: any recommendation that would increase the operator's margin or lengthen a commitment
dominance_rules.action: state the compensation model and the direct-purchase alternative in writing first, then make the recommendation

dominance_rules.rationale: a promise about a rule the operator has not verified is a liability that outlives the deal it won
dominance_rules.trigger: a client asserts a regulated data class or a contractual security requirement the operator cannot confirm
dominance_rules.action: name the class, route verification to the client's own advisers in their jurisdiction, and promise no compliance outcome while the question is open

dominance_rules.rationale: in a recurring book an unprofitable account is a standing subscription to loss with administrative duty attached
dominance_rules.trigger: an account prices below the measured floor, or logged support minutes show an existing account has fallen below it
dominance_rules.action: re-price transparently with a base management fee, restructure the service, or decline and refer; never restore the margin by adding licences the client does not need

dominance_rules.rule: The commitment term actually purchased dominates the cancellation flexibility the operator would like to promise
dominance_rules.rationale: the operator cannot execute a client's cancellation upstream against a term it has already committed to
dominance_rules.trigger: a client requests flexibility that the quoted term structure cannot deliver
dominance_rules.action: requote on the flexible structure at its true rate or state the committed term plainly; never sell a cancellation right that cannot be executed

dominance_rules.rule: Discovery completeness dominates quote speed for anything touching migration scope
dominance_rules.rationale: the scope drivers that decide a migration's cost are invisible from a seat count and expensive to discover on a cutover weekend
dominance_rules.trigger: pressure to issue a firm price before the discovery record exists
dominance_rules.action: issue an explicitly labelled budgetary range and make the firm figure contingent on the completed record, or quote a bounded emergency scope with a stated re-quote point

anti_rework_rules.rule: Choose the transacting route and confirm the attached support duty before quoting any per-seat price
anti_rework_rules.prevents: quoting a margin that the route's duties and costs do not actually leave behind, then discovering it after a book of clients has been priced

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the human, shared, alias and resource inventory before mapping anything to licences
anti_rework_rules.prevents: selling seats that are not people, then reissuing the quote and the invoice after the client counts their staff

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the suite-fit diagnosis before proposing any migration
anti_rework_rules.prevents: migrating a client whose real problem lives in domain records, a line-of-business application or a working habit that no suite change repairs

anti_rework_rules.rule: Re-pull the price list and term structure on the day a quote is issued
anti_rework_rules.prevents: committing for a full term to a margin the program had already changed before the client signed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Establish who has authority to authorise administrative access before promising a delivery date
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a signed engagement that cannot legally start, with a cutover weekend already booked and staff already told

anti_rework_rules.rule: Derive the setup fee from measured scope drivers before any discount is discussed
anti_rework_rules.prevents: financing the migration out of future subscription margin and losing the hours when the client leaves or is acquired

anti_rework_rules.rule: State inclusions, exclusions, ownership and the support channel in the offer before delivery begins
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unbounded support relationship priced at seat margin, and the argument about what was included that follows the first large request

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the disqualification rules before the pipeline fills rather than after the first bad account
anti_rework_rules.prevents: accumulating clients that must later be unwound, each with administrative access and a live subscription attached

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record every recommendation that reduced the operator's own revenue at the moment it is made
anti_rework_rules.prevents: having to reconstruct an advice trail from memory when a client, a partner or an adviser later asks why a tier was chosen

iteration_protocol.trigger: the vendor or provider publishes a price-list revision, promotion end or term restructure
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the dated terms register, recompute the margin worksheet, and re-check and reissue every outstanding quote before its validity date passes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a quarter of measured support minutes shows an account sitting below the cost-to-serve floor
iteration_protocol.action: recompute account contribution, decide explicitly to re-price with a base fee, restructure or exit, and tighten the decline rules for that class of prospect

iteration_protocol.trigger: a vendor renames tiers, moves features between them, or changes seat caps and eligibility
iteration_protocol.action: rebuild the licence map with fresh dates and re-check every client's right-sizing at their next scheduled review rather than all at once

iteration_protocol.trigger: a delivered engagement reveals a scope driver the discovery record never asked about
iteration_protocol.action: add the question to the discovery template and the driver to the setup fee derivation, and note the hours it actually consumed

iteration_protocol.trigger: a target segment stops responding or converts far below the others
iteration_protocol.action: re-rank the segments on observed response, rewrite the accountability message for the ones that do respond, and re-check whether the trigger watchlist still matches

iteration_protocol.trigger: a client challenges a recommendation as self-serving, or expresses surprise at how the operator is paid
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the disclosure and the recommendation log, correct whichever practice created the impression, and restate the compensation model in writing to that client and in the standard proposal

iteration_protocol.trigger: delegated access approaches expiry, or a client's authorized signer or ownership changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-issue the authorization record with the current signer and deputy, re-scope the administrative roles held, and remove anything no longer needed

iteration_protocol.trigger: an obligation class turns out to apply differently than assumed, whether through an adviser's answer, a client contract or a regulator
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the class in the client's jurisdiction, adjust what the offer and marketing may say, and update the decline rules if the class is now outside the operator's competence

priority_rationale: The frame and program work units come first because what the business sells, which route it transacts under, what the program obliges it to do and what its access duties are all determine whether any downstream number is real; targeting and suite choice come next because they decide which clients and which platform every later artifact is built for; the per-client units (discovery, fit, right-sizing, fees) come last because each consumes facts the earlier units define, and the offer is last of all because it can only mirror terms that have already been fixed upstream.
